text_fidelity_a:
10.1" Car DVD Player with Free Wireless Headphone Support HDMI Input, Sync Screen, AV in & Out, Last Memory, USB SD - NAVISKAUTO If you are looking for a portable DVD player that has intuitive controls, a remote control and a case to hold the DVD player so you can view the screen while seated in the back of a vehicle, this is a good choice. The screen swivels around so you can fold this in half "backwards" so only the screen is showing. This is helpful when using the case for use in a vehicle.

Compared to my regular TV this is an enhanced viewing experience. I found this to be a better visual experience. All the colors were vivid and almost velvety. Whether I am watching a favorite movie or a nature DVD, the colors are fantastic. Greens and yellows are super crisp and water looks totally glossy. I can't emphasize enough how beautiful the colors are on the screen.

I found many uses for this DVD player. It literally became my entertainment companion for two days while I tried out every feature. What I loved best was playing my virtual fireplace DVD with a beach fire and ocean waves. The stereo sound on this is excellent, I felt I was really at the beach which made me happy.

The remote control works very well and allows you to do things like turn the subtitles on or off. The audio controls let you choose between various options. You can stop or pause the movie you are watching either from the controls on the DVD player or by using the remote control.

This DVD player also has a screen saver that comes up when you put it on pause or don't turn the screen off. There is a button that says TFT ON/OFF that turns the screen off when you only want to listen to the sound. I found this played CDs too so that made me very happy. You can listen with the stereo speakers or use headphones.

If you are looking to view widescreen movies, this works for that too.

This is perfect to take with you when traveling. The only caution is not to use it for yourself if you are driving. It does have a cigarette charger that will work in cars and RVs.

The only thing I do when taking out a CD or DVD is to turn the DVD player off completely.

Some other uses I found for this DVD player was to play relaxing DVDs before bed to calm the mind. I also watched an underwater DVD with fish swimming by. This DVD player allows you to have entertainment wherever you are. The battery lasts about 4-5 hours, but if it starts to run out you can just plug the unit in and continue watching.

The only thing I noticed that was different than a regular DVD player was when you are halfway through a movie, put it on pause instead of taking out the DVD. This does not seem to have any memory of where you left off so when you put the DVD back in it just starts from the beginning again. This is not a big issue if you just hit the pause button.

I'm very happy with this DVD player and it is fun to go into your own little movie world. This is handy to have when someone else is using the computer or main TV. You can watch movies anywhere you want. I use this mostly when sitting in bed.

~The Rebecca Review

I received one free DVD player for review purposes.
text_fidelity_b: 10.1" Car DVD Player with Free Wireless Headphone Support HDMI Input, Sync Screen, AV in & Out, Last Memory, USB SD - NAVISKAUTO

text_fidelity_a: Echo Show 5 (2nd Gen, 2021 release) | Smart display with Alexa and 2 MP camera | Charcoal I purchased this recently for my son and I. The Echo itself seems great and does what it's supposed to do. My huge concern is who can drop in on my echo. Here's why I say this. My ex has an Alexa device and had full control over it while living here. I never had access to that account besides being able to talk to the Alexa. When I set this Echo up in my house all of a sudden his Alexa popped up under the communications tab. I don't have this person's number in my phone and I don't show any devices when I go into my Amazon account besides my new Echo. I can't find any option at all to block this person or get this person off my Echo. From what it looks like they can just drop in whenever they want which they had a bad habit of doing on their device when it was here. I find no way to remove that device without turning off the "drop-in" feature which is why I bought it so I can connect with my son if I'm not here. If there was a way to get this persons information off my Echo it would be a 5 star review, but since I have to worry everyday if they will just be able to drop in and be watching us or we won't know they are dropping in that's a huge thing for me. So if someone knows how to get them off it would be great if someone could tell me how that works. Otherwise, this rating will stay the same as I don't like not knowing if someone will be able to spy on us.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show 5 (2nd Gen, 2021 release) | Smart display with Alexa and 2 MP camera | Charcoal

text_fidelity_a:
Inspection Camera, AsperX Endoscope Borescope, 8MM 1080P HD Snake Camera with Front-View & Side-View Dual Camera 6 LED Lights, 16.4 ft Cable, IP67 Waterproof, 32 GB Card I used to have a cheaper one where you connect it to your smartphone, so when I saw this I grabbed it. I read two reviews where one said you cannot record 1080p, but the other said that you could. You know there are cheap cameras everywhere recording 1080p. For $90, I'm disappointed to confirm the reviewer who said this only records videos in VGA and snap pictures at 720p. 1080p is only for onscreen viewing. This won't be a big deal for me since I'm not in a profession that uses this daily. I figure it's nifty to have in the toolbox, and perhaps know my way around my walls. For example, last month I drilled a hole into my wall, thinking I can drop some cables down, but the cables hit a horizontal beam. I think in construction this is called a fire stop. Hopefully this will help me learn the paths I could take in my walls.

For a professional who will use this daily, who perhaps would like to bring back a picture or a video and blow it up on his monitor for a more detailed view, 1980's VGA quality is a big thumbs down! The build quality is also not substantial either. Everything is plastic. The whole unit is about 13.5 ounces.

I do like all the provided accessories, especially the hook. I can see how that will come in handy. To view something in the wall or pipe and to pry it out with the hook. The cable is stiff and bendable allowing you to position your lens just the way you want it.

IMPORTANT ADVICE REGARDING MICRO SD CARD!!!
------------------------------------------------------------
Be very careful when removing and inserting the sd card. You have to be sure to look at the slot, and be sure you slide the card in completely horizontal. If you slide it in at an angle, it will actually still go in, completely in! I made this mistake and the card was rattling around behind the LCD screen. LOL! Luckily, the screen was easy to take apart. Just 5 screws in the back and I was able to pry it in half and retrieve my card. When inserting the card, remember the orientation... with the LCD screen facing the ceiling, the card's gold contact side should also be facing the ceiling.

This is a 5 star product for hobbyist like me. I don't see myself recording much, if at all. For a professional, I think the shortcomings make it a 3 star product. So I'm rating this a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Inspection Camera, AsperX Endoscope Borescope, 8MM 1080P HD Snake Camera with Front-View & Side-View Dual Camera 6 LED Lights, 16.4 ft Cable, IP67 Waterproof, 32 GB Card

Renegade Concepts: Lap PRO - Stand/Caddy Universal Beanbag Lap Stand Tablet Accessory for iPad 1, iPad 2, iPad 3, iPad 4, Acer, Nexus & All Android Tablets, E-Readers, Books & Google Devices (Blue) The LAP PRO universal tablet stand doesn't work very well with my Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Wi-Fi tablet. The stand consists of a very firm, 18-inch wide, cylindrical pillow with a soft handle that doubles as a sort of tray for the tablet. Because there is no frame to hold the tablet securely, the tablet must be set carefully into the handle-tray, and then the tablet simply leans against the pillow for support. However, the tablet is very easily dislodged from the tray, even when the stand is sitting on a flat tabletop.

Out of the box, the LAP PRO holds the 8.9" Kindle Fire HD tablet at a near-vertical angle that is uncomfortable for viewing or for using a stylus on the touch screen. There is a sheet packed with the pillow that says: "Your LAP PRO has come slightly over filled intentionally, which may interfere with some functions. This will change in time. This is to ensure it will perform properly and last longer after it breaks in. The fabric will stretch and the beans settle from use." However, this is not really a beanbag stand. The pillow is filled with something that feels like medium-fine sand (not beans). Also, the pillow is too firm to accommodate its shape to an uneven surface the way a beanbag does.

To adjust the tablet viewing angle, you must reshape the pillow--it isn't enough to simply roll the pillow forward or backwards. Because the pillow is so firm, you must exert some effort in reshaping. It is easier to adjust the pillow shape and the viewing angle if you unzip the zipper that runs alongside the handle-tray, but then the pillow kind of flops around. (The zipper is there to open and close a compartment that is probably intended to hold your tablet, because the LAP PRO is also supposed to be a "caddy".)

If I needed a travel pillow (another of the LAP PRO's advertised uses) or a tablet caddy, I might end up liking the LAP PRO. However, because the stand is too large for convenient tabletop use, is hard to adjust, doesn't hold the tablet securely, and needs break-in time, I rate it at 2 stars ("I don't like it" on the official Amazon scale).

EDITED 11/18/12: After hearing from the seller, Renegade Concepts, I believe that I may have received an overfilled LAP PRO. (Renegade Concepts offered to replace my unit.) If my LAP PRO had been less firm out of the box, I would have rated it at 3 stars ("It's OK").
text_fidelity_b: Renegade Concepts: Lap PRO - Stand/Caddy Universal Beanbag Lap Stand Tablet Accessory for iPad 1, iPad 2, iPad 3, iPad 4, Acer, Nexus & All Android Tablets, E-Readers, Books & Google Devices (Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
ELECJET MagJet, Magnetic USB C Charger Adapter, 4.3A 87W Fast Charge, 6 Pin Reversible, QC 3.0 & PD, for New MacBook Pro/Air and Any USB C Devices (White) So far, very impressive. The magnetic breakaway connector is tiny, and its 87W-capable cable is lightweight and flexible-- way more so than the Apple USB-C charging cable that came with my 15" MacBook Pro and its 87W charger. It looks good, fully Apple-class in design and construction. But what sets this apart is a clever technical detail:

It uses a six-pin design approach that splits the charging current between two pairs of pins at the corners of the pin array, cutting the current through each by half. That is clever and I think unique, and it should make life easier on the port and probably on the Mac by reducing arcing and generally providing a better, more robust connection.

The magnet is nice and strong, and the L-shaped cable configuration lowers the torque on the connector, reducing unwanted disconnects while ensuring it breaks away when you want it to.

As with most USB-C charging cables and magnetic-breakaway adaptors, this is for charging only-- no data will traverse it. If you want a MagSafe-like adaptor that will handle both 87W charging and high-speed data, check out the Snapnator, also available here on Amazon. I have one of those too, and it's excellent, but it sticks straight out from the Mac and is more prone to disconnects, partly because I use it with the Apple charging cable that is so puzzlingly heavy and stiff.

My only issue with the design of this cable is that its strain relief construction is identical to Apple's, meaning the cable will eventually wear at the edge of the strain-relief. That's a common issue with charging cables and something we've all come to live with but it's still regrettable. I do wish cable designers would pay better attention to it, but it's universal, even with Apple's premium-priced cables.

The cable came in a nice little zipper case made of some sort of rigid formed fabric covered with a rubbery coating. Unfortunately there was a paper bar-code sticker on the case, and when I peeled it off, off came the coating. Ah well.

I'll post any updates over time.
text_fidelity_b: ELECJET MagJet, Magnetic USB C Charger Adapter, 4.3A 87W Fast Charge, 6 Pin Reversible, QC 3.0 & PD, for New MacBook Pro/Air and Any USB C Devices (White)

COO Case Compatible with iPad 9th/8th/7th Generation Case, iPad 10.2 inch Case with Pencil Holder, Protective Case with Soft TPU, Auto Wake/Sleep, Cover for iPad Case 2021/2020/2019 This keyboard is impressive. I'm using it with my iPad air 3 and its a perfect fit. The plastic is a little stiffer than some of the softer cases available, so getting the tablet to pop in and out requires a little extra effort and care, but once in, its solidly held in place and the whole thing seems very sturdy. When closed, it seems to offer very good protection, although, with the stiffer plastic, I suppose the case itself could potentially crack if subject to overly rough treatment.

As for the keyboard, it operates independently of the tablet... that is to say, it has its own on-off switch and it must be charged separately (in addition to the tablet). Since it connects via Bluetooth, it really doesn't need to be physically attached to work, just within Bluetooth range. (You could leave your iPad on a stand while typing on the keyboard in your lap, for example).

The keys themselves feel good, with adequate travel and response to the touch - you can actually "type" on it... although it is slightly smaller than a standard keyboard (as you would expect), its still comfortable enough for regular use. Also, there's a backlight for the keys which I kinda like... my laptop also has that feature and it makes it usable anytime, anywhere (out on the deck after the sun goes down, for example).

The fact that it can be twisted around and folded back on itself for simple tablet use makes it that much more usable. It does add a little heft to an iPad air, including some weight and some thickness, so if the thin form factor and light weight were key reasons for choosing the Ipad Air in the first place, this will negate some of that.

Personally, I like this keyboard - I intend to use it when traveling instead of lugging along my oversized laptop. Recommended.

It is quite thin and portable. It caught my attention because it supports pairing with up to 3 bluetooth devices simultaneously and with many of us having multiple devices (phone and tablet is quite normal), these devices are great for someone like me.

The clamshell design means that the keys are protected when closed. It also holds itself closed magnetically, and powers on my simply opening it. Pairing is easy: hold the function key and press one of the Q,W, or E keys to select one of the three bluetooth slots, then press the big "connection" button on the left bezel of the keyboard. This all seems pretty slick to me but I did have one concern with this keyboard's design and that is the hinge system. When the keyboard is open, it is quite easy to twist it with just a little bit of pressure. It means that I'm always extra careful when I'm taking it out of my bag.

In terms of functionality, the keys are a the same size as the ones on my laptop and has the same amount of travel as well, although they are a little bit louder than my laptop's keys when typing. I'm using this keyboard to type this review right now. What I found is that the keys are a little bit unresponsive. I keep missing letters every few words I type. Just in this last sentence, I had to go back about 5 times to correct missing letters. This defeats the purpose of purchasing a keyboard to type more quickly on a mobile device. Perhaps if you are normally heavy-handed when you type on a keyboard, you wouldn't face this issue.

Something that I wish this keyboard had is a touch pad. If this device can be both a keyboard and mouse, it would be much more useful.

Overall, the Samsers Wireless Portable Folding Keyboard is a good device but ultimately, it has a couple of shortcomings that keep it from being great.

text_fidelity_a:
Lowepro LP36915 ViewPoint CS 40 - A Soft-Sided Protective Case for a Smartphone, GoPro or 360 Camera and Accessories,Black Reviewed by my husband, a photography enthusiast.

Over the last 20 years, my husband has purchased several LowePro camera bags/backpacks (i.e., Mini Trekker & Micro-Trekker 100). He has found that they have been some of the best he has ever owned. He prefers backpacks because they are easy to carry and keep up with, especially if you are on the go. Backpacks also allow for easy storage and are super convenient. They give you freedom of movement and your hands are free to capture those special moments that you may not otherwise get if you were holding a bag in your hand. The Viewpoint (LowePro) BP 250 is the perfect addition to his bag collection especially since it is specially designed for small video equipment.

Here’s what he liked:

• This bag is attractive. The design is smart, functional and full of surprises. The Viewpoint BP250 is well-made with plenty of room for your Go Pro and accompanying equipment. There is a ton of storage (inside and out). There are several compartments where you can store your accessories, cords, lenses and other equipment. On the outside of the main bag, there is a zipper pocket (which allows for small items like a memory stick/card or thumbdrive). There is a pocket on the other side of the bag which will fit a small tripod or other item (like an umbrella). The entire bag can be zippered so you won’t lose any of your accessories.

• It is ideal for those who use (small) video and other digital equipment. There is a space dedicated to a small computer. While this backpack will not allow you to carry one of the larger sized laptops (our 17” didn’t fit), it has adequate space for the smaller ones (about 15”), a SurfacePro, iPad or other small notebook or tablet. He finds that the option of carrying a computer is great because it will allow you to quickly upload and edit your videos wherever you are. There is no reason to wait….just review, edit (if needed), and upload!

• The straps are unlike the traditional ones that come straight down the shoulders. The BP250 LowePro’s straps are curved which he found to be less stress on his shoulders. After some adjustments (he’s 6’1, average sized with average shoulders), it was a good fit. The straps are slightly padded and comfortable. There are small snaps that lock the straps in place to ensure that they don’t fall down when walking or hiking.

• There is a small (lunch box sized bag) that can be removed and can hold your GoPro camera and equipment. Once closed, it fits directly into your main LowePro Bag. It is padded and once inside, will protect your camera and smaller lenses. Or if you want, this smaller bag can be used instead of taking the large one.

• This bag comes with a rain cover. Not sure how much you will use this feature, but if you are ever caught in a drizzle or rain storm, there is a plastic cover that can be removed (unzipped) from the bottom and cover your bag. This is perfect for keeping your bag and equipment dry.

• The price. While this bag may seem a little pricey (about $130) it’s worth it. The craftsmanship and functionality will prove invaluable for the amateur or professional photographer. It’s a small investment with some heavy returns. You’ve got protection and functionality.

Overall, my husband gives this bag 5 stars. He finds that it is not only good to use for a GoPro, but other small video and photography equipment. Backpacks are useful for photographers because they allow your hands to be free to capture those moments or events as they unfold. In the past he has purchased Lowepro equipment and found them to be sturdy and durable, and the Viewpoint BP250 is not different. It looks good and he won’t leave home without it.
text_fidelity_b: Lowepro LP36915 ViewPoint CS 40 - A Soft-Sided Protective Case for a Smartphone, GoPro or 360 Camera and Accessories,Black

APC Power Strip with USB Charging Ports, Surge Protector P8U2, 2630 Joules, Flat Plug, 8 Outlets More electronics in the home means a need for more outlets. An ordinary extension cord will do the trick, but if you want something that looks nicer, has more functionality, and protects against power surges than one good option is the APC P11U2 APC Surge Arrest.

This surge protection device is great for those who need extra outlets for plugging in electronics and other things. It has eleven sockets plus 2 USB ports for a total of 13 places to plug things in and keep them running. An indicator light will tell you if there is an overload, which is highly possible when there are so any plugs. We don’t have this problem because we use this on our kid’s tech table. It allows them to plug in their cell phones, tablets, kindles, and other items- all which use minimal power- and get everything charged all at once without them fighting over limited outlet availability.

Each of the outlets on this surge protector has a safety closure, which is good for keeping out unwanted items. This can be useful if you have young children- wouldn’t want junior sticking a paper clip or other item inside one of the sockets. And a light glows to indicate that the surge protection is working as it should.

If I could change one thing about this, it would be the length of the cord. It would be better if it was just a little longer because it would be capable of reaching further. But other than that, this surge protector has worked just fine for my needs. It has ample space to plug in and charge all of our household electronics, keeping them ready for use and protecting against power spikes in the process.

text_fidelity_a:
Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch This bag arrived just before we went out of town for a trip, and the timing couldn’t have been better. My wife has a 13” laptop that she loves and uses daily, and this bag was the perfect solution for carrying it on the trip. It isn’t necessarily the most fancy bag but it gets the job done and it seems to be made well. I would make one alteration to make it better, based on experiences I have had with similar bags in the past.

This is a smaller bag, not designed to hold 15.6” or larger laptops, so it is not going to help people who have “standard” laptop sizes unless this is going to be used as a book bag instead. If you need a bag that fits a laptop that is 15.6” or greater, this one will not work for you. That’s okay as it is very clearly marketed as such so it should come as no surprise. Being for smaller computers doesn’t make it useless though; it does work very well as a book bag and an organizer, so even if you need a larger one for your computer this one has its uses.

This is a leather messenger bag. The leather is a style I have heard referred to as “ruined leather” though that’s not an indicator of the quality. On the contrary, this bag is well made and I can’t find anything about it to suggest that it is made with less care and quality than the price dictates. In spite of the appearance, the materials are quality and I cannot find any blemishes or cuts, the stitching is straight and all the clasps and zippers work properly.

There are plenty of pockets to store your items and keep organized. Of course there this the main compartment which is designed to hold a computer, but there is room for books as well in the main compartment. There are zippered compartments inside the bag as well as outside, and these are good for carrying your mouse, pens and pencils, passport, maps and other important items.

The flap that covers the main compartment secures to the rest of the bag with straps that fasten with a pressure snap behind a fake decorative buckle, and this represents the one thing about this bag I do not like. If you are not careful and you catch one of the straps on something will walking, you can break the snap and damage or ruin the bag. I have had this happen with other bags using this kind of fastener. I would rather see a magnet used instead which will let go when pulled, or get rid of the decorative buckle and replace it with a real buckle which will hold regardless.

I like this bag. It is well made and it should last for years with proper care. It has room for your smaller laptop as well as books and other supplies. I don’t like the way the flap secures, mainly because if problems I have had with similar bags using similar fasteners, but for the majority of users this is a good solution that is worth consideration. It’s a little more expensive than a canvas bag, but it should last longer.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch

text_fidelity_a:
Seagate Wireless Plus 1TB Portable Hard Drive with Built-in WiFi (STCK1000100) I intended to give the [[ASIN:B00AQRUW4Q Seagate Wireless Plus 1 TB Mobile Device Storage with Built-In Wi-Fi Streaming (STCK1000100)]] a rating of four stars, but have decided that it really is a five star product. The near deduction was because of the frustration I experienced in my attempting to get the device up and running with the limited information provided in the package and on the website. Once I successfully downloaded the software to my Droid, Kindle Fire and MacBook, I still encountered more trial and error than usual until I was able to figure out how the darn thing works. Fast forward to days and weeks of loving the device!

The Wireless Plus can be used as an extra drive for storage if you're not interested in using it for streaming, but if that's your true need, I'd likely recommend purchasing something else. With it's own Wi-Fi streaming, you don't need to use your home or hot network. Using it's Wi-Fi has been quick and has been glitch free for us thus far. We have used three devices at once and found it to be problem-free, with no freezes, crashes or difficulties. We had it up and running for four hours and still had battery power, then recharged. Although it can be charged via the USB on your computer, it is much faster by plugging it into an electrical outlet if one's available. Since we haven't drained the battery yet, I can't say how long it really lasts.

Music, movies, pictures, documents, audiobook, you can use whichever you want on any networked device as long as the device has the appropriate application installed. I watched the Seagate tutorials several times and found them to be difficult to follow, however once I spent some dedicated time just feeling my way through, I discovered that I do like the applications, too. Even if I'm not accessing the Wireless Plus on my Droid, I have been using the Seagate app.

This arrives with little documentation, but it is USB 3 capable if you need it. The housing is lightly rubberized and it has a matte metal plate in a charcoal gray color on the face side. The plug appears to be proprietary, the second reason I almost deducted a star from this review. It looks like a hybrid mini plug that's attached via a thin wire, not a cable, to a USB for either a device or the two prong electrical plug. No case is included, but I have a couple that work great. The size isn't so big that it feels cumbersome, but it is heavier than it appears to be upon first glance. I don't mind the weight because this little device holds 1 TB, much more than I have loaded on it as of today. I highly recommend this device and look forward to Seagate upgrading it as time passes. It's unique and not expensive for what it offers.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate Wireless Plus 1TB Portable Hard Drive with Built-in WiFi (STCK1000100)

IOGEAR 2-Port USB DVI-D Cable KVM Switch - 1920 x 1200 60Hz - 2.1 Audio w/Mic - USB 2.0 Peripheral Sharing Via Mouse Port - Hotkey or Remote Switching - Plug n Play - Win/ Linux / Mac / Sun - GCS932UB What a great way to work on two PCs from a single set of Keyboard, Monitor, Mouse, Speakers and Microphone. This product is so easy to install and works perfectly! The length of the cords is pretty much perfect, so I can station my two towers well away from each other and thus avoid heat buildup, which could happen if they had to be positioned too close to one another.

I would suggest only one or two small improvements to make this setup work even better. I would label the switch itself with A/B tags, and I would also put two, different colored LED lights on each end of the switcher, which would each light up, depending on which computer one is working on. That way, the user can quickly visually identify which computer is currently in use, instead of trying to guess.

I have put A/B tags on my switcher and on my respective computers too. However, since the switch is not a toggle switch, I often still have to figure out which computer I am working from when I don't remember where I left off the time before.

Otherwise, this device seems to perform seamlessly. Just remember that when you are rebooting one of the computers, be sure to keep the peripherals connected until they are recognized. Otherwise, when you toggle back again, you may find a screen with very large graphics on it - like I did once. I just had to reboot and stay with that computer until I saw the Windows welcome screen. After that all went fine.

I have a Windows 7 computer and an XP connected to this. My peripherals are HP w2007 Monitor, Altec Lansing VS2521 2.1 Powered Speaker System, Microsoft Natural Ergonomic Keyboard 4000 v1.0 (USB) and a Logitech Cordless Trackman Wheel (USB). Have not yet tried my Logitech USB Desktop Microphone.

Great product at a very nice price. I recommend it highly!
text_fidelity_b: IOGEAR 2-Port USB DVI-D Cable KVM Switch - 1920 x 1200 60Hz - 2.1 Audio w/Mic - USB 2.0 Peripheral Sharing Via Mouse Port - Hotkey or Remote Switching - Plug n Play - Win/ Linux / Mac / Sun - GCS932UB

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation Back in 2016, I was getting into the Video Doorbells for extra security for packages. After much review of Ring, Skybell, Nest, and August doorbells, I decided to purchase the Skybell. I instantly enjoyed being able to get notifications when there was motion and when the button would be pressed. The advantage with Skybell was that it came with free subscription. Well... after 2 years of using the Skybell, i ran into many issues where the motion would not notify me or even pickup, wireless trying to connect to my network at home, and many other headaches which you would think be fixed after many patches. I have my own server room and network system which I ran network throughout my house and even have a business hotspot near the Skybell, still had many issues with the Skybell doorbell.

Moving forward......

I reviewed my options again as I was fed up with Skybell and still only had the same options today as they were 2 years ago. After much consideration i decided to choose the Ring Doorbell 2. They do offer a free subscription now, which is great, but you cannot review any motion or button press history events. Of course this is just due to needing to purchase the basic plan for the cloud storage. Even for $30 annually, the basic plan is still cost effective. After using the doorbell in the trial version of the plus plan, I am planning on paying the $30 just because its cheap cost and I would rather have the events to review rather than just seeing the live view.

Setup was easy (easier than Skybell). The app loads quick and can edit motion detection's, alerts, and much more. I connected the doorbell via hardwired to an analog doorbell. The box comes with many customization options, tools, and took only 10 minutes to install.

Testing the Ring doorbell worked perfectly and better than Skybell. I installed my Ring doorbell with the provided wedges that came in the box. I have a 20 foot driveway and the detection works so great that cars driving by alert me. You can decrease the range of the motion in the app. When there is motion, I can open the app from my lock-screen and only takes about 2 to 3 seconds before i can see the event. The load times are very quick and faster than Skybell.

Overall, I am day 15 in my trial and I am glad I decided on Ring. The product is great, and far better than competitors. Cost is ideal for those that do not want to pay hundreds each year on cloud storage like nest. I would highly recommend Ring to others.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation

text_fidelity_a:
Large Print Backlit Keyboard, Quiet USB Wired Computer Keyboard, Full Size Keyboard with White Illuminated LED Compatible for Windows Desktop, Laptop, PC, Gaming, Black I had a keyboard die when I spilled liquid on it so I grabbed the first one I saw available without looking at the details. When I opened the box and found that this was a backlit keyboard with large print keys, I was intrigued. As an old, retired guy, I spend hours a day at the computer gaming, streaming videos, and staying in touch with a far-flung network of family and friends via social media. This keyboard is particularly nice for the gaming. The white backlight against the black keyboard, as well as the large print keys make it very easy for me to hit the right keys when my eyes are bouncing back and forth between the screen and the keyboard while my hands are handling the both the keyboard and the mouse. This keyboard makes my responses faster and more accurate, which I very much appreciate as an older gamer.

There are those irritating glitches though. One of the worse is that the backspace key constantly sticks. Thankfully, I don't use that key in my gaming, or this keyboard would be totally unusable for me. When typing things like this review though, or posts on social media, that sticky key is very frustrating. Every time I have to backspace to clear a mistake I have to hit that key repeatedly, like I had to do three times while typing this sentence. What makes it even worse is that there is no telling how many hits it takes to move back the necessary amount of spaces. So it is very easy to backspace too far, causing even more mistakes.

Another glitch is that the keys seem bigger than on my last keyboard. I don't notice that in gaming, but when typing more than a few sentences of text, my hands and fingers begin to feel some strain. There are some minor glitches too. The volume control on my speakers is in an awkward place to reach. My last keyboard had separate volume control keys, making it easy to adjust the volume from the keyboard. This one also has volume controls but they are on the function keys, requiring two buttons to be pressed to raise or lower the volume. That sounds like a small thing but every time I adjust the volume,it is a bit irritating to have to hit two keys instead of one. And finally, this keyboard bills itself as "quiet". Hah! It's probably the nosiest, clackity clack typing I've done in a long, long time.

All in all, this keyboard feels like a cheaper knockoff of a higher quality one. For now I'll use this one, because I need it. As soon as I find that higher quality keyboard though, this one is getting tossed out.
text_fidelity_b: Large Print Backlit Keyboard, Quiet USB Wired Computer Keyboard, Full Size Keyboard with White Illuminated LED Compatible for Windows Desktop, Laptop, PC, Gaming, Black

Rii (Newest Version) K12+ Mini Wireless Keyboard with Touchpad Mouse, Stainless Steel Portable Wireless Keyboard with USB Receiver for MacBook/iPad/Tablet/PC/Laptop/Smart TV/Raspberry Pi - Black It helps to have small hands to use this small keyboard, and I almost got used to scrunching my hands together to type with it. Until I needed to enter an underscore. The -_ key should be located to the right of the 0 key. Since high school that's where my right hand is trained to go for that key. But on this keyboard it's two keys right of the space bar. What???? Keyboard manufacturers really need to stop rearranging the keys we've all learned to locate on a standard keyboard layout. I know compromises sometimes need to be made for a small form factor, but this is really a deal-breaker for me, so I'm returning. I also found the touchpad precision to be below average even after tinkering with the Windows mouse settings. Ehhhhh.

UPDATE: I checked the product photos, and in the first two pictures the -_ key is in the expected location, but in the next two pictures the -_ key is in the awkward location as it was in the keyboard I received. Granted, on the box it says "THE MANUFACTURER RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AMEND THE SPECIFICATIONS WITHOUT PRIOR NOTIFICATION. THE PICTURES AND DATE IN THE STYLEBOOK ARE FOR CONSULT ONLY IF THERE IS FLUCTUATION..." (Not sure this is a "right"... sounds more like an "adopted business practice" to eschew product configuration management). Well, I reserve the "right" to return for refund a product that isn't the same as what's in the pictures.

So in other words you might receive the product shown in pics 1-2, or pics 3-4, or something different.

Disclaimer: My negative review starkly contrasts with the glowing 5-star reviews from the many reviewers who received this product free in exchange for a review. However, since I PAID FULL PRICE for this item, my standards may admittedly be somewhat higher.
text_fidelity_b: Rii (Newest Version) K12+ Mini Wireless Keyboard with Touchpad Mouse, Stainless Steel Portable Wireless Keyboard with USB Receiver for MacBook/iPad/Tablet/PC/Laptop/Smart TV/Raspberry Pi - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google I have had the opportunity to review a few similar products over the last couple years and this new security light by Sentry has some great features that make it a stand out among other security lights.

I found installation straightforward and simple. For those who have trouble connecting to your WiFi, the most common issue is the strength of the different frequencies your router is broadcasting. The easiest way to resolve this is to go into your router settings via your computer and turn off the 5 GHz band during setup. This is necessary sometimes when initially setting up SmartHome products. While some may find this necessary for this product, I did not using my Orbi router system.

The Geeni App is easy to use and makes setup and customization of how the light operates user friendly.

This unit puts out a huge amount of light - 2100 Lumens to be exact while only using 24 watts of power thanks to it utilizing the LED bulbs.

This is the first security bulb I have reviewed that actually has a built in siren. This could be an outstanding feature if needed. Whether utilized to scare off someone attempting to break in to your home or to cause unwanted pests to run the other way - it will work! This siren is effective because it’s loud.

The speaker can also be used for communication purposes. By utilizing a built in microphone you’ll be able to have conversations with those you are viewing through the camera. The speaker and microphone have a surprisingly high clarity. The only thing I found odd with this aspect of this product is this is not a light you’ll want to place at head height as the light is so bright and the camera is really made to provide a wide angle view. Therefore when you speak through the speaker I found people usually look around and can’t figure out the source of the disembodied voice.

After using this product for the last 6 weeks I have found that it performs excellently. By installing a 128GB micro SD card within it, saving videos is easy and I’ve had plenty of time to review the footage. I love that it holds the recording locally so there is no cloud subscription fee required.

This is an excellent security light that will not only light the night when motion is detected, but will record it, alert you, scare the intruder with a siren or allow you to speak to them (or apologize for just scaring them with the siren).

This is an outstanding product that I definitely recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google

VIZIO M-Series All-in-One 2.1 Immersive Sound Bar with 6 High-Performance Speakers, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, Built in Subwoofers and Alexa Compatibility, M213ad-K8, 2023 Model I CHOSE this model over another because of the supposed built-in Alexa compatibility. You can indeed connect the soundbar to an Echo device *as a regular bluetooth connection*, but the instructions to enable Auto VA (auto virtual assistant mode) via Bluetooth so the soundbar maintains a BT connection with Echo while using other inputs DOESN'T WORK. The instructions say to first connect the soundbar to Echo via BT (✅), and then to press the Bluetooth button for 10 seconds to enable Auto VA (❌). HOWEVER; after five seconds, the soundbar enters Bluetooth pairing mode. I've tried dozens of times, connecting and disconnecting the BT connection with Echo and restarting and resetting the soundbar: NO DICE.

It's frustrating because this feature is in the title of the product and is clearly described in the User Manual — and yet it doesn't work at all.

I imagine Auto VA via AUX input works okay, but that means I have to move my Echo or get a wicked-long audio cable, neither of which I want to do.

However, otherwise the soundbar sounds fine. Not quite as good as the Bose Companion computer speakers I used previously, but whole worlds better than the built in TV speakers. It's just a shame that I have disconnect and reconnect to Alexa so often.

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMC-LX3 10.1MP Digital Camera with 24mm Wide Angle MEGA Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Black) The wide angle lens is wonderful. The field of view and the speed (light gathering ability) of the lens can only be rivaled by high end camera and lens combinations costing six to ten times as much (admittedly those are superior in many other ways as well). Still, the point is that no other compact point and shoot camera can rival the field of view and speed of this one. Nevertheless, some things come up short of fair on the LX3.

The shutter lag is terrible. I am a very instinctive shooter that is quite capable in photojournalist style candids but I am almost always defeated by this camera.

I am not a photophile or electronic gadget spec sheet bench racer. I've done wonderful 8x10 prints with a 6MP camera and 10MP is enough to get prints after substantial cropping. I have huge film scans when I need them but I cannot realistically show dozens of megapixels on screen or in print for more than a handful of images. I also shoot in .jpg and it's great. I can't imagine the agony of terabytes of raw data jamming my PC.

I love the LX3 video quality for movies. It's ideal for Youtube and even Youtube HD. I do not like the Quicktime .MOV format or the weak compression algorithm. I wish it had H.264 and wrote an .MPG type format. It still beats the data format from a DVD camcorder though.

The audio quality for movies is terrible. Again, I'm not talking audiophile critique here. For comparison, my Sony DSC T9 (ultra compact point and shoot) has far better sound.

I hate the manual aspect ratio slider. If I shoot movies I want 16:9 but for stills I want 3:2 (of course). The LX3 requires that I remember to both turn the dial and slide the switch or I will end up shooting 16:9 stills.

Overall, it's a great camera. I hope they get the rest sorted out by the time I expect to buy another one in about 3 or 4 years.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMC-LX3 10.1MP Digital Camera with 24mm Wide Angle MEGA Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player) Since we mounted our TV we like to use as few chords as possible. This way they are neatly tucked along the wall and down into the entertainment center where all our entertainment equipment is housed. So the main HDMI cable runs down but of course we have more components that require a cable than the one connected to the TV. Our solution? A signal splitter. Thankfully, we have only three output connections so this one seemed perfect. Plus, it touts 4k signal, even though most pre-4k HDMI boxes should be fine, but it's nice to have that in the title just in case.

What I use this mostly for is the cable box and a couple of video game systems. As for the cable box, seems to work fine; no dropped signals that I've noticed, nor any degradation in quality. As for game consoles, I have the PS3 and the Wii U hooked up to it. SAme: no noticeable quality degradation nor input lag.
Now, to put it to the real test, I hooked up some retro consoles that have been modded to output native HDMI; that means they'll be HDMI with no lag. Considering I have this and two HDMI cables connecting the console to the TV, I was curious to see if there truly was any lag.
With older games, timing is everything, especially on the 8-bit consoles with platformers and fighters, like the NES. From what I could tell, there was absolutely no lag, not to mention signal loss. The buttons responded as though I were using a normal NES on a CRT.

So yeah, I'm pretty satisfied. It's a bit light and doesn't have heavy pads on the bottom to prevent it from sliding around. With so many cables, and the ability to use the remote control, it should be a bit more stable on the surface.
I haven't used the remote as the detections are instant. No need to manually switch the inputs, at least from my experience. Also, I didn't need to use the power adapter; the power from the HDMI cables seemed to be sufficient, and the detection was not complicated by the lack of adapter. Weird.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player)

text_fidelity_a: WD 8TB My Book Desktop External Hard Drive, USB 3.0, External HDD with Password Protection and Backup Software - WDBBGB0080HBK-NESN Buyers should note that this drive is formatted in exFAT. Without knowing this, I plugged it in to a running computer and began to transfer some files. The computer was shut down for the night. The next morning, I found that the computer refused to boot up with the new drive installed. Unplugged the drive, and the computer booted up fine. Finally checked the file system. Found it to be exFAT. Moved the files off and re-formatted the drive to NTFS and the problem went away. I suggest anyone purchasing this unit just save yourself the time and trouble and reformat it right out of the box. The software on the drive isn't needed anyway. I have several Western Digital external drives and this is the first one that arrived in a format other than NTFS.
text_fidelity_b: WD 8TB My Book Desktop External Hard Drive, USB 3.0, External HDD with Password Protection and Backup Software - WDBBGB0080HBK-NESN

text_fidelity_a:
ECLIPSE PHOTO GROUP Front and Rear Professional Lens Protectors As someone who works with cameras for a living, I tend to occasionally misplace/lose my lens caps. Having a one-size-fits-all backup like this claims to be, is therefore intriguing to me.
What I found however, is that this fits alright for smaller sized primes (such as those with a front element of 52mm), but a lot of my zooms or larger primes with bigger front elements are difficult or impossible to fit over. Rear cap was also somewhat of a hit-or-miss; I own E-mount, EOS, Nikon F, Minolta A-mount and Micro4/3 lenses, and none of them are too large in their rear element, but some lenses get wide right after the mount and won't allow a cover like this to squeeze over easily. Some of the smaller primes, especially pancake lenses like the Canon 40mm STM, really can't fit both a front and rear "cap" like this since the entire lens would be engulfed in one end or the other.
On top of all that, even if it DOES fit over your lens, I'm cynical as to how how useful it really is. The purpose of a lens cap is to protect the glass from two things: getting dirty and getting damaged. For starters, the material is soft and won't prevent a hard object collision. I'm not exactly willing to test that theory but considering I can press in and feel the glass through the cover, I'm guessing a hard object in your camera bag could still hit it and crack/shatter/damage it. Perhaps the rubber would soften the blow, but a real lens cap would prevent any blow from happening in the first place!
For dust and debris protection, perhaps it is a little useful, however this sort of material tends to attract a lot of static cling. Just leaving it in my gear bag for a bit, I'm finding dust and hair clinging to it like a balloon. Now, it is possible that means the dust/debris will stick to the cap and not your lens, which is useful, however it doesn't give me a lot of confidence to see stuff stuck to the thing I'm about to use to protect my lens from more of that stuff.

I suppose it's good as a backup in my gearbag in case I lose another lens cap and want something to keep dust off it until I get a replacement, but otherwise I'd strongly recommend getting a proper front and end cap for your lenses.
text_fidelity_b: ECLIPSE PHOTO GROUP Front and Rear Professional Lens Protectors

text_fidelity_a:
RCA Digital Amplifier for Indoor Antenna I "Cut the cord" and got rid of my satellite service recently, but did miss watching network TV. Consequently, I bought a Mohu Leaf TV antenna. It works well, but I added this amplifier to see if I could pull in more channels.

Short answer: For me, this amplifier works. It added 10 channels to my lineup. There are several caveats: The effectiveness of this amplifier will vary depending on your location and distance from a major city. (I'm about 60 miles from Denver.) My reception does vary depending on the weather, which can be maddening. On a good day, I can get a total of about 40 channels. Many of these channels (almost half) are religious, Spanish and shopping channels that I don't really watch.

Without the amplifier, I get about 30 channels. I have found that moving my Mohu Leaf around on the wall will improve my reception for certain channels. The important thing is to experiment to see what works for you. Check out the excellent resources online for working with an indoor TV antenna. And think of all the money you are saving!
text_fidelity_b: RCA Digital Amplifier for Indoor Antenna

text_fidelity_a:
Sony SRS-XB12 Mini Bluetooth Speaker Loud Extra Bass Portable Wireless Speaker with Bluetooth -Loud Audio for Phone Calls- Small Waterproof and Dustproof Travel Music Speakers Gray SRS-XB12/H [[VIDEOID:bbb3e1079eb39e7b0d0221b2e128e01d]] I am not an audiophile; however, I know great sound when I hear it, and this tiny speaker delivers crisp, clear sound. I would expect nothing less from Sony. However, it is a little bright with more midrange and treble and it sometimes sounds a little thin. The bass has a little bit of thump and does not distort even with the volume maxed out.

I used an audio cable with my Echo Dot and Bluetooth with my phone and computer.

Steely Dan is my test music, and my EQ is set to flat so I can hear what this speaker is capable of without the help of any adjustments.

I made this video using my largest audio file on my MacBook Pro. You can be the judge.

The only things I do not like are the controls, and I think the volume is lacking. I have the volume set to max on both the speaker and my computer. It can fill the small area I am occupying, but not the room.

It's a very compact speaker, and I think it sounds tremendous when you consider its size. The clarity is impressive, and it does not distort. Overall, I am pretty happy with the sound quality and I would have rated it higher if the price point were lower. At the time of this review, it costs $50 and there are a lot of great speakers at nearly half that cost. If it could produce the same sound clarity with more volume it would be worth every penny.
text_fidelity_b: Sony SRS-XB12 Mini Bluetooth Speaker Loud Extra Bass Portable Wireless Speaker with Bluetooth -Loud Audio for Phone Calls- Small Waterproof and Dustproof Travel Music Speakers Gray SRS-XB12/H

Amazon Basics 6 Outlet, Wall Mount Surge Protector, Power Strip, 2 USB ports 3.4A, 1080 Joules This AMAZONBASICS 6-OUTLET WALL MOUNT SURGE PROTECTOR (with 2 USB ports 3.4A, 1080 Joules) installs easily--all you need is a screwdriver (flat or Phillips). The surge protector is rated 1080 joules, which is much more protection than you get from most inexpensive surge protectors. This is plenty of protection for the power surges that happen when the power goes out and is restored suddenly.

Because my power company (PGE) delivers a LOT of unexpected power outages, I need surge protectors on all household outlets that service expensive-to-replace electronic equipment (e.g., microwave oven, coffeepot, TV, toaster).

This wall mount surge protector works well in my kitchen, where I have several small appliances that I like to leave plugged in. It also expands a standard 2-outlet wall outlet to 6 outlets. (This is okay, because I don’t plug kitchen appliances into all 6 outlets at once.) The surge protector has an orange light that tells you it is working. If the orange light goes out (for example, after a sudden power outage), then the surge protector needs to be replaced.

The two USB charging outlets are nice to have, but I don’t need them in my kitchen. If you don’t need these, you can buy a cheaper AmazonBasics model that is the same except that it omits the USB feature.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics 6 Outlet, Wall Mount Surge Protector, Power Strip, 2 USB ports 3.4A, 1080 Joules

eufy Security Indoor Cam E220, Pan & Tilt, Indoor Security Camera, 2K - 3 MP Wi-Fi Plug-in, Voice Assistant Compatibility, Night Vision, Motion Tracking, HomeBase 3 Compatible, Motion Only Alert Purchased two of these Eufy 2K cams to test out and determine if they're good enough to replace the Wyze cams. These Eufy cams definitely capture higher resolution, more detailed videos compared to the Wyze cam v2. The pan and tilt feature is great when I want to remotely check different parts of an area and the pan/tilt action is very silent. You can set the cam to automatically track/follow motion when it's detected. The amount of time it takes to go to live view on a cam is within a couple of seconds and the alerts for motion is definitely faster than the Wyze cam v2. The time from me waving my hand in front of the cam and getting an alert on my phone is about 3 seconds or less.

I did experience issues with one Eufy cam where it would randomly start panning by itself and would do a 360 degree pan. The Eufy app works overall, but I did notice several times I had connection issues when trying to live view, but this issue also happens on Wyze cams, too.

You can set the Eufy cam to record only when motion or sound is detected or set the cam to continuous recording. If you choose continuous recording the video resolution will be reduced to 1080p resolution. For motion recording you can set up activity zones (specific areas you want to detect motion), adjust motion detection sensitivity, detect people, detect pets, and detect all other motion. Eufy's app is still missing the ability to view multiple live views of cams at the same time, which is a shame and hopefully they have a software update for that.

Overall, the Eufy 2k cam has great video quality, the pan/tilt motion is useful and silent, has a lot of features, and the price is competitive. They go on sale from time to time, so if you're not in a hurry then I'd wait for a sale.

Monoprice VGA to RCA Adapter PC to TV Video Converter- Blue Ok... I KNOW better than to purchase any electronic gizmo with less than a four star overall rating. I took a chance this time - I was looking for a cheap way to stream video on my television via the computer without having to buy a Roku etc. This converter thing SHOULD have worked fine. I guess, technically it works, but not the way I needed it to and honestly, it's just a HUGE hassle to use on a regular basis.

Pros..... it's small. It does send the video to the television (you do have to tell your computer to send the data to another monitor). It was inexpensive.

Cons.... Our 3 year old tv has all the connections for stuff - USB, S-cable, that 3 prong thing, 3 HDMI outlets and it connects easily & streams Netflix via the Wii game box. It works with the DVD player and I've played DVDs through the laptop in the past with the USB connection, so I KNOW they all work. The ONLY way it would work with this converter box was to use the S-cable and the yellow prong cable AND the USB all at the same time. The picture qualtiy was fine. I tried for 20 minutes to get the sound to transfer through to the television - never happened. Which meant I had to leave the laptop speakers on in order to listen to dialog. Not conducive to sitting several feet away from the screen. Meanwhile there was a huge tangle of all these cables on the tv stand, the laptop, low sound and no ability to pause etc without getting up and going to the computer to do it manually. By the end of a single episode of Frasier (23 minutes) the little converter box was very hot to the touch and the wood underneath it was hot as well. I imagine if you watched a full length movie you might end up scortching the finish on the tv stand or table!

End result.... I'm returning this converter first thing in the morning. I'll just cough up the money and buy the ROKU I guess.

The amplifier which comes in the box with this antenna actually made the signal worse--not better, so I disconnected that.

Give the few number of channels that actually come through, on hindsight, I would have bought a much cheaper antenna. It does not pull in channels more than about 20 miles away. Even channels 20 miles away aren't received.

Otherwise, the reception on the channels that do come through is great.

All of this may be because I am in an old, downtown neighborhood, with close houses and lots of trees. Although I installed it in an area of the roof free of trees.

JAM XT Extreme Wireless Speaker, Splash Proof, Drop Proof, Dirt Proof IP64 Rating, Carabiner Clip, Built-in Speakerphone, Works with iPhone, Android, Bluetooth Devices, HXP430BK Black I will give you the down and dirty in short bullet form. Hopefully this answers most questions.

PROS of this product
* Easy to set up and use.
* Quality of the sound is good and it isn't heavy on the bass. Music is clear. The one speaker (mono) gives off great sound.
*Item is portable and sturdy.
*Item has Bluetooth function or you can hook it straight to your device. (I used my son's cord from his VModa head-set to connect to my android. ) Otherwise I used the Bluetooth function on my IPAD, IPOD and Nexus 4 (android phone) with no problem. The range or reception is decent. I didn't have any breaks in the connection, but I really didn't try to go too far. I tend to stay in the same room or in the general area, while listening to music.
*You can control the sound from your device or from the speaker. AND you can still pause your music using your device.
*Easy to charge. I really liked the fact that it is compatible with any USB or android charger. Meaning if you have an Apple device (ex., IPOD or IPAD), etc you can use the charger to charge this speaker. Or at least use the base portion of the charger. If you have an android, you can use that cord as well. The charge life for the battery is reasonable, and it even comes with a lithium battery.
*You can attach it to a book-bag or backpack (as shown in the photo), but I just place it where I want it to be and put it down. It is small enough (about the size of the palm of my hand) to fit into any purse, or bag without making it too heavy. Basically you can use this anywhere (in the home, camping, on trips, at the beach) and at any time.
* It's cute (I have the black. It kind of looks like a smashed soda can). Again, it's small. There are controls and indicator lights on the bottom of the device. The charge area is located on the top.
*Price seems comparable with other products of this sort (wireless speakers) on the market.

THINGS I WOULD CHANGE (not really a CON) about this product:
*The USB cord could be a bit longer. It was a little short for my tastes. But at least it's versatile.

So, as you can see, I was pleased with this product. The PROS definitely outweigh the "things that I would change" category. It had everything that made this a winner. It was easy to set up, and has decent sound quality. I definitely would recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Asus Transformer Pad Infinity TF700T-B1-GR 10.1-Inch 32GB Tablet (Amethyst Gray) I debated for a long time about getting a tablet. A couple years ago I'd have sworn that I'd never have one. I've been a laptop guy for a long time and love the PC, but it gets cumbersome some times. You can't do everything with a tablet that you can with a PC, but for most people it can fill most of your needs. Smart phones are nice but they're just to small for my eyes and big fingers. Besides, my view of cell phones is something to make calls with and talk on.

That said as I read and looked at different tablets, I realized the potential for their use. I've got issues with Apple and didn't want to go the ipad route for a number of reasons. I did some research on the new Windows tablets and I like the idea, but they've got a way to go. I think they rushed it to get it to market. I like the ideas behind Android and although a lot of the apps are designed more for smart phones, apps optimized for tablets are increasing and all the other smart phone designed apps work. The open source design makes for all sorts of obscure market apps. Plenty of developers out there. You can find some weird stuff for Android that you won't find on other platforms. Lots of pretty good free apps and plenty of cheap stuff too that is impressive.

So next I had to decide on size. For 99% of my uses, the 10 inch seemed to be the better choice and with a number of these with docking key pads available, I went that way rather than the smaller versions. So then I had to decide which one. It didn't take long to realize that ASUS was probably the leader in the field and known for very high quality products. Likewise it only took a bit longer to see that the Infinity TF700 with 64GB, was the machine to have. I also opted for the docking keypad.

The tablet is very impressive. The screen resolution is right up there with the best ipad. The NVIDIA quad core CPU is a screamer. Can't get much better. Cameras are very good. Battery life is good and amazing with the dock which also has a battery in it. With all the features together, I think this is the best Android tablet out there today and most pro revues agree.

As a new user to this scene, I'm sure others may have different ideas that got me to this choice, but I can say that I am completely satisfied. That said, as a "newbie" I suppose you might think anything would seem that way, however, I did a lot of research and hands on comparisons and I'm comfortable I bought the best.

I am 99.9% thrilled with it. If it has a flaw, it's probably the speaker which faces the wrong way in my opinion and doesn't have quite the volume and sound quality I'd like. It is fine in a quiet environment, but if there's any background noise it leaves a bit to be desired. I have found that if you hold it with your hand somewhat loosely cupped behind the speaker, the sound level improves dramatically as your hand reflects if towrd you. It is fine with ear buds and I also recently picked up a great little bluetooth speaker, (Clalrity HD by Monster), that kicks butt.

Everything else about the Infinity TF700 seems perfect. The only other way to make it better would be built in 4G and phone capability. If I'm mobile I use mine with a Verizon Jet Pack, which is an awesome device itself. Even on 3G it works better than my built in mobile broadband in my laptop.

Do your own research and get some hands on time if you can to compare because all tablets are not equal. There is no doubt that as far as tablets go, a lot has to do with how you will use it and what for. But if you want the best Android tablet in the 10 inch size range, you can't beat the Infinity TF700. This thing is awesome!
text_fidelity_b: Asus Transformer Pad Infinity TF700T-B1-GR 10.1-Inch 32GB Tablet (Amethyst Gray)

Followed the included instructions exactly and lined up the screen protector with the Fire's camera etc and laid it down. The package had a stiff cardboard piece that works better than a credit card to smooth the protector sheet as you go - I have no air bubbles at all on the first try. Once it's in place, you need to remove the blue top layer to reveal the actual clear screen cover you will be looking at and touching when you use your tablet. The use of any screen cover is going to diminish the clarity of your high definition video, that's just a fact of life. This one is no exception. But...it does cut the glare in direct sunlight and it really helps prevent scratches to Fire's screen which means I can use my Fire in more places than before and in turn makes it more valuable to me. text_fidelity_a:
PANASONIC Bluetooth Wireless Headphones with Microphone and Call / Volume Controller - RP-HF400B-K - On-Ear Headphones (Black) I have worked with a lot of Bluetooth headphones, all of which have their strengths and weaknesses. These headphones by Panasonic are on the less expensive end. The question is whether they are worth the asking price. In my opinion, they could be better and are still priced a little high.

Comfort-wise, I do not care for these but this is a personal preference. I like a headphone that fits tightly and presses down on my head, and these are very light-fitting. They adjust well enough and there should not be too much trouble getting these to fit almost any head, but keep in mind that they’re not the type that clamps down tightly.

The build quality is sub-par. These are very lightweight and feel quite flimsy and fragile.

I found an issue in the sound profile. The bass is good and not too heavy, and that’s good news for me. I dislike strong bass which is good for giving me headaches. The midrange is on target too and the music has some depth. Where the problem lies is in the highs. When listening to music I noticed some distortion in the highs. It’s not in-your-face and it doesn’t ruin the listening experience unless you are really fussy about your music. These will be fine for listening to speech, though.

I had no trouble connecting these to my laptop via Bluetooth. These come up quickly and connect without any issue and are ready to go in seconds. These aren’t the absolute fastest connecting phones I have worked with but they are among the faster ones I have used.

There’s no protective case for these phones in the box, not even a sleeve. These do fold up nice and compactly but I am not sure what is the point without a case in which to store them.

As I write this, the asking price for these phones is $60 which is a bit high in my eyes. If the sound profile was perfect, or if the build quality was higher, I would be more amenable to that price but the truth is that less expensive phones can be found that have a better sound profile and are constructed more solidly - and they have a case.

These are not bad phones, but I think they leave much to be desired. The build quality is mediocre, the sound profile is imperfect and the cost is a little high for what is in the box.
text_fidelity_b: PANASONIC Bluetooth Wireless Headphones with Microphone and Call / Volume Controller - RP-HF400B-K - On-Ear Headphones (Black)

WD_BLACK 1TB SN850 NVMe Internal Gaming SSD Solid State Drive with Heatsink - Works with Playstation 5, Gen4 PCIe, M.2 2280, Up to 7,000 MB/s - WDS100T1XHE I originally bought a WD 2tb NVME to use as my main OS, but it would not migrate/clone properly even with their own software. I downloaded a 3rd party migration/cloning software and that didnt work either. I tried nearly everything I could for 1.5 days! I even tried backing up/restoring manually and then repairing. Nothing worked. It was a complete waste of time. I didnt even learn anything in the process other than learning that I should go with a company that has a readily available comprehensive solution that doesn't needlessly waste your valuable time. 1.5 days down the drain.

So I ended up migrating my Samsung 1tb NVME to a new Samsung 2tb NVME and it couldnt have been any easier. < 15 minutes, very quick! I previously, migrated from a corsair SSD to Samsung 1tb NVME (when i couldnt get another SSD to migrate properly), and that was flawless as well. Why didnt I initially go with the Samsung 2tb instead of WD? Press had positive news about it. I am not a fanboy so I like to try different solutions. That was a mistake. What's apparent to me after this experience is that Samsung is better than all their competitors at providing a comprehensive package of the best hardware and software. The experience is FLAWLESS. I havent had any issues with any of their storage solutions to date.

Why did I bother writing this review? Because I wasted 1.5 days. Something has to come out of it. Maybe itll help someone or maybe WD will get their act together and work on their cloning/migration software because the hardware seems to be fantastic.

Disclosure, I bought and paid for everything myself and I still own HDs/SSDs/MicroSds by WD (only old HDs), Sandisk (microsds, ssds), Seagate (HD), Samsung (SSDs, Micro SDs and NVMEs).
text_fidelity_b: WD_BLACK 1TB SN850 NVMe Internal Gaming SSD Solid State Drive with Heatsink - Works with Playstation 5, Gen4 PCIe, M.2 2280, Up to 7,000 MB/s - WDS100T1XHE

ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).
If you want to spring for the subscription service, there's a TON of goodies and advanced features beyond even the cloud storage things. But even without that, the live view and photo motion alerts combined with the voice assistant / Alexa integration makes it worth it even just for the hardware alone!
text_fidelity_b: ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In

text_fidelity_a:
42 Inch/106CM Light Reflector 5-in-1 Collapsible Multi-Disc with Bag - Translucent, Silver, Gold, White and Black for Studio Photography Lighting and Outdoor Lighting I ordered the 43 Inch/110 Centimeter Light Reflector. It comes in it's own little zippered bag. The fabric appears to mostly be nylon, so it should wash easily with a damp cloth. The stitching is solid. I didn't know what to expect, but the Light Reflectors are exactly as pictured. My only little gripe is I had to refer to the listing to remember how to fold it to fit back into the pouch. Once you remove it, you have a large disk, silver on one side, black on the other. This has another zipper on the side. Inside the reflector's zipper is a diffuser which you will need to remove from the larger pouch to use. This is where the mounting tab is located. You will need the mounted clip that is available as part of the kit, or you may purchase it separately. That's not all. The large, outer pouch is reversible, so you then reverse the large pouch and you have a gold reflector one one side or a solid white on the opposite side. This is how you have black, white, gold, silver and a diffuser all in one. The diffuser has it's own tap to clip on your tripod, which pokes through from a button hole to mount the entire piece. You will need to make sure it's pulled through if you remove the outer layer of the reflector.

This is a good purchase for the value. I'm a hobbyist, and sometimes take photos of my projects. My problem comes from being a night-shift worker. I live and work at night. I must make my own lighting setup if I want to photograph anything at night, even in my home. It's light weight, and folds to a small circle, so this is also portable. It weighs less than a pair of jeans.

Here's a free tip: Only use the gold if your subject is brown. I don't find the gold reflector so useful. I'm glad it's available, but I doubt it will get much use for me. Also, place the reflector in a way that would mimic the sun's light, and your subject will look more natural. This is where the clips and extension arms from your tripod can come in handy if you are working solo. Of course, you can always enlist the assistance of another for outdoor shoots. Sometimes this is a best option if it's available. In the movies, they tend to show someone holding a reflector with it facing up towards the subject, but that's only because it does look silly holding a big disc over your head. If you hold it, you will need to hold it up over your head, and it will look silly but your photos will not.

It's a good tool to have on hand for any level of photography. I mostly photograph my doll collection. Once or twice a year, our doll collectors group will gather outdoors for shoots. We've not had a reflector available to us before, so this will help us immensely finding good spots to make photographs, even if the clouds are moving or we want to setup under trees.

I also ordered the 2-pack clips. These are nice because they come with an adapter on them. If you remove the threaded black female cylinder and threaded ring, you are left with a standard sized male mount that will fit a tripod base. You do not need to make a separate purchase for an adapter, it's already there. The ball joint swivels all the way around and there is a groove in the base to tilt the clip in towards the base, so you can use these clips for holding the reflectors, diffuser or even a backdrop on a side or top mount adapter of your backdrop frame.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.
text_fidelity_b: 42 Inch/106CM Light Reflector 5-in-1 Collapsible Multi-Disc with Bag - Translucent, Silver, Gold, White and Black for Studio Photography Lighting and Outdoor Lighting

text_fidelity_a:
CoolBELL 17.3 Inches Convertible Laptop Messenger Bag Shoulder Bag Backpack Oxford Cloth Multi-Functional Briefcase for Men Women Laptop/MacBook (Blue) First and foremost, I need a convertible backpack which allows for transport - all materials needed for the long days on campus (grad student). In addition, I need the professional aspect to function as a briefcase. Solely on those points, this bag fits the bill. (BTW - no discount or freebie here for this review - I paid for this!)
PROS:
1. Material: feels and looks professional, good color, seems at the very least to be water repellent
2. Zippers: seem strong enough, especially when loaded - two of them house the briefcase handles
3. Padding: quality - on the backpack straps and particularly the section directly meant for the computer
4. Compartments: although the pictures do not necessarily show this, there are zippers on the outside, and inside, a pocket with divisions for pencils/pens/highlighters.

CONS:
1. Backpack adjustable straps: are on the lower part not allowing for easy adjustment while on your back
2. Lower connection backpack straps: hidden - cannot see whether sewn in well or not
3. Strap to hold computer in place: oddly long, which would allow for movement and sliding around, something you don't want your computer to do when inside
4. No compartment/pocket for a water bottle (my pet peeve)
5. PRIMARY (HUGE) ISSUE: Backpack straps which rest on upper trapezoids (left and right) are situated in a very uncomfortable position when fully loaded. I'm unsure if it's the angle or the placement, but the straps are too close to your neck and would cause pain. Primarily for this reason, I'm returning the backpack. Sad because even with the other cons (more annoyances than anything else) if it were not for this one, I would've kept the backpack because the pros outweigh the cons.

Pictures: It's important to see how a backpack will perform in my daily life. Therefore, the pictures provide a sense of how much stuff this can carry, with the contents both packed and unpacked.

Contents: Lenovo ThinkPad T460 in neoprene case, keys, 1 1/2" loose-leaf binder, yearly planner, scientific calculator, computer power cord, small cosmetic case, large cosmetic bag which houses pens/pencils/highlighters/usb drive/mouse/headphones and wallet.

Final thoughts: if only used as a briefcase/shoulder bag, this may be for you. However, if the primary purpose is to function as a backpack, good luck. I think another reviewer mentioned the oddly-placed backpack straps, but sadly, I ignored that advice.
In addition, cannot ascertain the strength of the shoulder strap as I didn't want to break the seal, but it is pictured.
text_fidelity_b: CoolBELL 17.3 Inches Convertible Laptop Messenger Bag Shoulder Bag Backpack Oxford Cloth Multi-Functional Briefcase for Men Women Laptop/MacBook (Blue)
