While most security cameras can be run via WiFi, nearly all of them still require a power adapter be plugged in. By utilizing this hub, security breaches are all but eliminated - by utilizing Ethernet instead of Wifi transmission your local storage unit makes it so there is no easy out of network access. In addition, transfer speed, resolution and picture quality is greatly increased - making the entire system more useful. In my experience, I found power is much easier to manage utilizing this method as opposed to having to run separate power supplies to each camera.

I have found this switch is rock solid and perfect for use as an unmanaged PoE switch for security cameras.

This is an all around outstanding product that I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend. This unit is sure to hold up well and perform even better.

text_fidelity_a:
GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) 4G LTE OpenWrt VPN Router, T-Mobile ONLY,128GB Max MicroSD, 7000mAh Battery, OpenVPN, WireGuard, Tor, a Router That You can Program (EP06-A), for North America only I love GL.iNet. They create routers based on OpenWRT, which has so many great features that you'd find in professional level routers that cost thousands of dollars. There is a fairly steep learning curve to it, though. Fortunately, GL.iNet understands this and makes things easier by creating their own customizations to the firmware to make OpenWRT easier to use and more custom to the routers themselves.

The GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) is their latest 4G LTE router. Pop in a sim card and the router will create a hotspot that routes to the LTE network. For additional protection, it is easy to set up the router to connect to a VPN provider. By connecting the router to VPN, all client computers connecting to it WIFI will be protected.

I used this router during my last trip and it was GREAT. I have a few devices that I bring with me. A laptop, tablet, and phone. I even bring a firetv with me sometimes. While in the car, I have the router connecting everyone's devices to the Internet via LTE and when I got to the hotel, I connected the router to the hotel's wifi and turned on VPN. The transition from LTE to hotel wifi was seamless. Not only did I not need to reconfigure everyone's devices to connect to the hotel WIFI, we were also secure behind the router's firewall and VPN connection.

The two restrictions that this product may present to potential buyers is first, the price. It is quite pricey and it can be hard to justify its purchase. Especially when you can get a travel router for around $40 with the ability to tether a phone via USB. The second issue is that this specific router is tied down to the T-Mobile network with no ability to unlock it for other networks (according to the seller's response in the questions section of for this product). If the convenience and the ability to fully control the TTL to bypass t-mobile's tethering throttling restrictions is important to you, it may justify the price you'd be paying.
text_fidelity_b: GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) 4G LTE OpenWrt VPN Router, T-Mobile ONLY,128GB Max MicroSD, 7000mAh Battery, OpenVPN, WireGuard, Tor, a Router That You can Program (EP06-A), for North America only

The fact that these phones are fairly neutral across the entire frequency spectrum makes them ideal for listening to unmixed recordings, as well as music that you are studying or transcribing. The reproduction is so balanced that listening to albums with these compared to other phones - including some other Brainwavz models - is like night and day.

If you are listening to music that is heavily biased towards bass and drums these may not be the best phones for you. If you listen to acoustic music these are near perfect because you can easily hear every note. I tested it on a few jazz albums that I own as well as a broadcast of two friends from a local station that had been recorded directly from the sound board and it was wonderful to hear what was actually recorded versus what a biased pair of phones normally reproduce.

A few notes about comfort: these are light, do a great job of isolating ambient noise without totally eliminating it, and are easy to wear. I am not an IEM (in ear monitor) type of person, but these presented no problems even when I wore them for three to four hours straight. A big plus is this set comes with different sized foam ear pieces and a nice case (the [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]).

While these phones may not be for everybody, they are perfect for those of us who spend a lot of time critically listening to music and/or transcribing it. If you fall into that category you will probably love them.
text_fidelity_b: BRAINWAVZ S0 in-Ear Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones Clearwavz Remote & Microphone Stereo Headphone Headset for iPhone iPad, iPod & Android Devices (Black)

D&O LIGHTING LED Video Light Panel – 180W Bi-Color Studio Lighting for Video Recording Filming with 97+ CRI - Aluminum Construction, Big Heat Sink Fins and On-Light V-Mount Adapter Plate for Battery I work in photo/video for a living, and I can tell you that good LEDs aren't cheap. I have worked with hot tungsten lamps for high output and smaller LEDs for lightweight smaller setups, but LED lights that can compete with the output of Tungstens are pricey.
That being said, this is a FANTASTIC light. It has high output yet has the pros of LED panels such as lower power consumption and heat, as well as being dimmable and color adjustable from the panel or remote control. I had the opportunity to use this for a job yesterday setting up an interview in an office setting. My tungsten bulbs would have been too bright and need gels to match the rest of the office. My other smaller LEDs would have cast smaller spots and we all know a larger light source casts a more pleasing glow. It seemed effortless to get the amount of light we needed in a short time.
HOWEVER, I did find that the mounting point was a little bit difficult to use. There are two bolts to secure it to the stand, and both need to be loosened to mount it properly. It took me a few attempts to get it on the stand, one side felt like I was screwing the bolt the wrong direction most of the time. Meanwhile, the light is large and kept wobbling during this overly complicated procedure. It didn't feel like a premium product during that, which I found odd considering the price point. I have lights that cost about half of this one that felt more premium during mounting. But, that being said, once the lights are up it works a treat!
So, a solid 4 stars from me. Almost 5 if the mounting were easier or the price lower to make up for that. But as a light, it does what it should do and well.
text_fidelity_b: D&O LIGHTING LED Video Light Panel – 180W Bi-Color Studio Lighting for Video Recording Filming with 97+ CRI - Aluminum Construction, Big Heat Sink Fins and On-Light V-Mount Adapter Plate for Battery

Logitech Wireless Desktop MK 300 This is the first Logitech keyboard I've gotten, and now I see why Logitech is considered to be a proficient manufacturer in keyboards and other computer-related paraphernalia.

Without installing any such programs or software, either from the website or from the included disc, I plugged in the USB receiver right out of the box, followed the easy-to-setup instructions engraved on the back of the keyboard, and away I went. I was able to type flawlessly at the office, and the keys are very smooth and quiet. Even though it's just a keyboard, I kept opening up different programs to test out the typing. Pure joy! (For a nerd like me, at least.)

I guess the only gripes I have, and I noticed it almost immediately, is that there are no lights to indicate locks for the numbers, caps, or scroll. It's a minor gripe, but a gripe nonetheless since I have to utilize the Caps Lock every so often at work.

When I used the extra buttons for various computer software, I found that the respected programs opened up right away. There was some stall, but that was the result of my slow, crunching computer.
The mouse worked just as it should.

Now, I have to admit, what I really wanted to get this keyboard for was my Wii at home. I know, it sounds nerdy.
But the keyboard I was using before was an old office wired one that was given to me. That one worked fine, but I wanted a wireless one. So, I took home this MK300 keyboard and USB receiver, plugged in the latter into the back of my Wii console, opened up the Internet Channel and found, to my delight, that the keyboard worked flawlessly.
There was some range betwixt the keyboard and receiver--about ten feet or so--but it made no matter: my sitting spot isn't too far from the console, so it's not like I'm going to be typing in a completely different room.

Since this keyboard works so well, I was hoping to use it on a Mac. I've yet to buy the MacBook Pro--which is why I'm stuck with the Wii's Internet Channel for now--and since the specifications for this certain keyboard doesn't include Apple's OS, I'm assuming that there is simply no way around hardware setups (ever tried?) and will have to resort to something else, when the time comes.

All in all, though, if you're looking for an excellent wireless (not Bluetooth) keyboard at a relatively inexpensive price tag for any PC machine or Wii, look no further. The MK300 works like a charm.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Desktop MK 300

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Voyage E-reader, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Adaptive Built-in Light, PagePress Sensors, Wi-Fi It's just plain spectacular how good the Kindle Voyage is.

I'm kind of a gadget junkie. Whenever a new Kindle reader comes out, I pass on the old one and buy the new. So I'm coming from a place that has used everything from the old Kindle Keyboard through to this, my newest Kindle, the Kindle Voyage 3G.

First, screen quality. I knew it had 300 v. 221 PPI I had on my PW2, but until I saw it, couldn't believe how much of a difference it made. Now, the PW2 screen is great, but this beats it soundly. For regular reading, I don't see any reason to switch from a PW2 to a Voyage, but I'd imagine that with illustrations and such, it would make a really big difference. I can actually read at one size smaller font than I could on the PW2.

The light: Nice light, no weird shadings. My device is smoothly lit from bottom to top.

Size/Weight: It's smaller, definitely (not the screen though). Couldn't really see any difference in weight between this and the PW2, but honestly, what's an ounce either way, especially once you start sticking covers on it? It's not something I particularly care about.

Storage/Memory: I wish it were a bit bigger. Not that I have any desire to have 2,000 on my Kindle at any given time, but once you get into using about half the memory, these devices always slow down and get ornery.

Wishes/Dreams for the next e-reader: That they'd include text to voice. I doubt this will happen, but I wish it would.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Voyage E-reader, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Adaptive Built-in Light, PagePress Sensors, Wi-Fi

So far it has met my expectations. There is some room for improvement but in operation it is a solid performer.

This is a very simple and straightforward thumb drive with no bells and whistles. It doesn't come with a cap, it doesn't extend/retract, and there isn't even an LED to indicate that it's working. However, it has been reliable up to this point and I have had no issues with transfers. The lack of an LED is mildly problematic because it is difficult to know when a transfer completes, but there are ways to work around that.

Speed is excellent. This is the fastest thumb drive I have now.

The lack of the LED, not including a cap or making the sleeve retract, and no lanyard are cut corners. All of these would make this a better product.

I am not unhappy with this drive and will use it until I wear it out. It is fast and appears to be reliable. It would have been nice if SanDisk had done more than the basics, but what is here is solid.

I like the feel of the keys on this keyboard - the rubbery surface is nice; the bumps on the F, J and 5 keys are easy to feel. The lighted keys look very cool in the dark, and have a good, solid feel when I press them.

What I don't like:

~ The lights in the keys are too dim. You can barely see them in a lit room. There should be a way to adjust the brightness of these lights.

~ The Num Lock, Cap Lock, etc. lights are too bright. There should be a way to adjust these also.

~ The Keyboard sits at too low an angle for my taste - the back feet of the keyboard should be raised higher.

~ The smooth finish of the area around the keys shows fingerprints horribly. This surface should be matte.

All in all, I like the keyboard (and will keep it), I just wish that a few things about it were designed differently...
text_fidelity_b: Razer Lycosa Mirror Gaming Keyboard - Special Edition

text_fidelity_a:
Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue *UPDATED REVIEW*

A seller replaced a different defective FM transmitter unit with this one for me (mine has the Kollea brand name on it, but this is the identical unit, private-labeled). This is a better product than what it replaced, but is not without it's flaws. I have three (*UPDATE: now four, and the fourth one is a deal-breaker--see below) complaints with this unit:

1) It will not automatically reconnect to my phone about 75% of the time. I have to manually shut Bluetooth off and turn it back on on the phone, sometimes a few times before it pairs successfully. This is a hassle--a PITA. Every time I get in the car, I have to go through this process--every time power is cut from the transmitter, actually, so if your passenger knocks it and it pops out of the 12V socket, it will have to be re-paired, which is supposed to happen automatically, but does not, and you then have to go through the process. Frustrating.

2) Charge output is only 1.0A. this is why I returned the first one--phone gives a "slow charging" warning when charging from this unit, regardless of what USB cable I use (I tried four different cables, all of which I know for certain can carry 2.1A).

3) Callers have occasionally complained they cannot hear me well when using this unit, and I occasionally (but not often) encounter FM interference. I believe Bluetooth itself is part of the problem, and anyone who has used a few Bluetooth headsets or units like this knows audio quality is terrible. Period. We just deal with it. Add to that the burden of having to transmit your signal via FM to a car stereo and the user-side audio (what you will hear in your car) is always going to be craptastic.

4) (*UPDATE) When paired, voice recognition on my phone, which is usually quite good, becomes severely impaired. This is also likely the culprit for complaint #3, above. I suspect this is because when paired, it tries to use the built-in microphone for voice recognition instead of the microphones on my phone (of which there are 4). It is disabling the extremely good microphones in my phone (Nokia lumia Icon which is well known for having incredible audio input) and using the unit's crappy microphone instead. This microphone is located in the unit, which is attached to the center console of my car near the shifter, and thus picks up all the vibrations and related road and engine noise transmitted through the structure of the car as I drive. This approach is terrible. I have stopped using the unit for anything requiring voice input, including telephone calls. In other words, this is just a big awkward charger now, and one that charges painfully slowly (see complaint #2). If it were possible to disable the onboard mic, and use the mics in my phone instead for calls and voice recognition, this would be a much more serviceable unit As it is now, it is just a piece of junk.

Cannot recommend this item. There are definitely worse products out there. I have not tried them all, but of those I have used, this is the best one so far. I will likely keep using it until the lack of automatic pairing pushes me over the edge with it one day and I get something else. (*UPDATE: this thing just does not work well, and I am now looking for something else.)
text_fidelity_b: Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon 7237 Action 7x35 EX Extreme All-Terrain Binocular These binoculars are all about quality in the largest field of view. If you want to see a wide expanse of nature or the heavens downrange from your position, these are the way to go. I got them specifically to frame smaller constellations and asterisms, the detail of which can be further examined with a scope. They help tremendously to put the object in the scope into context. Ordinarily, observing half a degree of field tends to abstract objects almost entirely from their surrounding. Since it's not practical to really "zoom" in using a single optical instrument, using these in combination with something of higher power is ideal. Don't get me wrong, I do have a zoom on the scope... it zooms from 25x to 50x -- amazing but you have to understand that this is a field of view of 2.4 to 1.5 degrees -- essentially like looking through a pipe to a drinkstraw. These Nikons however, show over 9 degrees field of view -- something which is unsurpassed in the highest-end binocular out there.

There are compromises necessitated by the optical principles used to make these function. They do not have a very flat field of view, meaning objects in the center of the field (circle) can be focused, but objects nearer the edge of the field are out of focus. This is because the focused field is curved not flat. This problem is also evident in most 10x50's for example. It's less of a problem in good quality 8x42's like Nikon's Monarch for example, and obviously the high end Swarovski, Leica, Zeiss etc. This problem matters more when you have a narrow field and highly magnified image where the subject tends to fill the field of view. It matters less when the subject is focused in the center of the field and the background surrounding it is slightly out of focus.

Still, even if you pay the biggest bucks for bright, flat, and sharp images from the top of the line binoculars, you'll still only see about 8 degrees true field of view, whereas these give you over 9 degrees. Furthermore, they give an apparent field of view of over 59 degrees, rivaling the top-of-the-line binoculars.

If you're looking for a handy, all-purpose binocular, the roof-prism 8x42's are proven to be far more popular for a number of good reasons (more compact, more magnification while not yet needing a tripod or IS like 10x does, more competition and choices etc.) But if you're looking for the best field of view with high quality optics, this is it, and fortunately it comes at a very reasonable cost. I don't know what other 7x35's are out there, but I can tell you this is far better than Celestron or Bushnell.

text_fidelity_a:
GoPro Hero — Waterproof Digital Action Camera for Travel with Touch Screen 1080p HD Video 10MP Photos NOTE: There are several models of GoPro cameras attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the GoPro Hero.

I have worked with a number of the cheap knock-off sport cameras available and up to this point I have been relatively satisfied with them. I have not worked with an actual GoPro before now, so I was interested in seeing how well this unit would compare to the cheap clones. There’s really no comparison – the GoPro is an order of magnitude better. Yes, it’s more expensive but it’s a higher quality product that works better.

Of the GoPro models available, this is the most budget-friendly I have seen and it doesn’t come with a lot of frills and extras. It does come in a waterproof shell and it does have a clip so you can attach it to a helmet or handle bars, but that’s really about all that comes in the package. There’s no memory card with it, either, so plan on picking up a MicroSD card with the camera.

The usability when compared to the cheap clones is about the same. The menus are a bit different but they do perform the same general functions. That said, where the GoPro Hero sets itself apart from all of those cheaper cameras is in the quality of the product and the resulting pictures and recordings. This little camera is solid and so is the waterproof shell; it will stand up to some abuse and should just keep right on going without batting an eye. It also produces better-quality video than every clone I have tried, which is saying something because some of the cheap cameras actually do a decent job of producing good video.

The size and weight are nice features that make it very highly portable. I have seen motorcyclists on the highways with cameras similar to this one mounted on their helmets, and while that looks funny to the observer it makes for some great videos online and it does give the motorcyclist some backing when there is a traffic incident. For the younger crowd, it’s great for capturing skateboarding tricks in the first person as well as that wild ride down a water tube.

I have not worked with this camera a whole lot yet but I have seen enough to know it’s a big upgrade from the cheaper clones that are available in abundance. The Hero is a budget-friendly option for the user who wants quality results without breaking the bank, in exchange for giving up some of the less critical features like Bluetooth and WiFi connectivity. If you need those features, but you still want the best-quality, you’ll need to look at one of the more advanced and expensive models.
text_fidelity_b: GoPro Hero — Waterproof Digital Action Camera for Travel with Touch Screen 1080p HD Video 10MP Photos

The power switch has three positions -- Off, On, and Auto. In the Auto setting, it turns itself on if it senses an incoming signal. When I'm playing music softly, I'm finding that it takes a while to discover that it should turn on. In my case, the subwoofer is sitting next to my desk, and it's not hard to reach the power switch. But keep this in mind if you want to hide it somewhere that would make the power switch hard to reach. (It's near the top of the rear of the cabinet.) There's also a phase switch, with two positions. There's no magic to that; just set it to the position that sounds best. As with all subwoofers, the placement in your room isn't critical, although the subwoofer's sound can be somewhat amplified if you locate it in a corner.

Update: I've had time now to use this with lots of different types of music, as well as TV and movies. The bass is very solid and tight, with no boominess at all. It blends beautifully, with plenty of power for my medium-sized room. This is very musical, adding firm support that's more than just "punch". This is surely one of the best values in powered subwoofers, and I'd buy it again in a heartbeat.
text_fidelity_b: Polk Audio PSW505 12" Powered Subwoofer, 460 Watts(300 Watts RMS) & Amazon Basics Subwoofer Cable, 25ft

TBMAX Portable Reading Light Gooseneck Tube Dimmable Desk Lamp with Adjusted Clip-On Stand, Touch-Sensitive Switch, Adapter, and 3 Brightness Levels, 2.5W - White I received this is a free review sample. For the price this is a bargain, but there are two things that kept me from giving it five stars. First is this does not use a standard micro USB style cable for charging. That means that unless you can find an easy source of cables with USB A on one end and the barrel connector this one has on the other, you are stuck with a three foot limitation of cable length. I have USB micro cables that are double that, and would have made this light all the more useful. Also, since I am using this as a music stand light if I misplace it for a gig I am out of luck because I do not own a similar charging cable (although I always have spare USB micro cables in my gig bag.) If you intend to use this as a fixed table lamp the cable issue will not be the problem for you that it is for me.

Second, the gooseneck is sensitive. If I bump a music stand with this light clamped to the shelf it will move far out of place. It's not stiff enough to hold if you do plan to use it with a music stand. For tables, bed stands, etc. it should work fine, though.

Here are some of the strengths: the lowest setting of illumination is perfect for stage use or if you want to read in bed without waking your partner up. At the highest setting it is definitely bright when lose in (about 1.5 meters), and - as Goldilocks said - the medium setting is just right.

Another feature is untethered to the charger this will operate for three hours at the brightest setting and half more than double that at the lowest. That means that if you are camping, on stage (or in front of a lectern) without a power source nearby you can still use it.

Finally, the included wall wart has a 2 Amp port for phones and tablets, as well as a 500mA port for charging this light. That is handy and all the more reason why the cable style for this lamp is a frustration - it could have easily been a five star product, and especially at the going price.

I work from a home office and got a treadmill desk for Christmas and needed a wireless keyboard so I can move it back and forth between the treadmill side and the keyboard tray on the other half of the desk for when I'm seated. I got so used to a split ergonomic keyboard and had difficulty finding this style in a wireless keyboard.

This is low profile enough to fit under the desk when I slide the keyboard tray out of the way. You can use it with or without the very easily magnetic attachable riser to raise the wrist rest; I use it without the riser when on the treadmill and with it when I'm seated so this is a great feature for me. I suppose it is somewhat equivalent to using the legs on traditional keyboards.

A large part of my day is spent on the phone with executives and I often type while talking with people (conducting telephone interviews). This keyboard is so much quieter than my old one! Now people don't even know that I'm typing while speaking with them. It did take me a day or two to get used to the keyboard layout since it is a bit different from my old wired ergonomic keyboard.

The mouse seemed too big initially but now I really like it.

I use the number keypad a lot and having it separate from the keyboard is sometimes not the most convenient. However, if it was attached to the keyboard, the set up would be too big for my keyboard tray and mouse so it is more of a positive than a negative with the new treadmill desk set up.

Overall, I am very happy with it and recommend it wholeheartedly. You will especially like it if you are used to using an ergonomic keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest.

text_fidelity_a: Fire TV Stick streaming device with Alexa built in, includes Alexa Voice Remote, HD, latest release I got the newest 4K streaming stick with alexa voice control remote. As of yet i haven't purchased a 4K T.V. but the firestick works on any high def T.V. with a hdmi port. There are lots of free movie and T.V. apps so you can cut the cord and save lots of $$ doing away with cable. You will just have to simply connect a OTA antenna to the back of your TV to receive your local channels. The remote is ok but not great. It does sync easily with your T.V.s CEC control and lets you use the remote for T.V. power on and off. Volume control and alexa voice command. But personally i found it just as quick and easy to manually navigate the apps you want to watch rather than using the button on the remote to ask for a certain app. More times than not the voice control will get what your asking it wrong. But the volume control and power control on the remote is a very good plus over the basic remote. The battery compartment for remote is a little tricky to get opened at first but if you just apply a slight pressure at the same time as sliding the compartment down jt will slide right open. And getting to the streaming quality it will depend on which app you are using. Surprising to me is that the Amazon Prime Video app uses a lot more wifi data than most of the other apps making the shows and movies buffer quite a bit sometimes. I am curious why Amazon Prime uses so much more data vs Netflix or Hulu for example but it surely does. And if you have a Roku device and are used to the Rokus functions it will take a bit of getting used to how the Firestick apps are downloaded and stored compared to the Roku. But they both have equally good and bad comparisons when it comes to their individual functions. Both have excellent picture and sound. What i would really like is for Amazon's firestick to have a remote control app for your android or ios phone. Roku does have the free remote app to download and works great navigating and also has alexa voice control and tou can plug earphones into your phone for private listening. And also remember when buying a firestick to check the gift box if it is going to be used by someone else in their home. If you check the connect to my account box instead all of your information on your other firesticks will be on the new one and also the Amazon buying app with your personal information. So be vigilante and at least have a PIN set up on your Amazon account so no non approved purchases can be made.
text_fidelity_b: Fire TV Stick streaming device with Alexa built in, includes Alexa Voice Remote, HD, latest release
